full_prompt_html:
Act as an experienced financial controller and FP&A analyst who writes management commentary for executive readers.

Write the variance commentary for this month’s management accounts. [Paste this month’s income statement, the budget and the prior-year figures for the same period, or attach the workbook.] [Paste any notes on one-off events, timing issues or known changes this month.]

Build the commentary in four parts:

1. Materiality and Scope

  • Calculate the variance to budget and to prior year for every line, in currency and as a percentage.
  • Comment only on lines where the variance exceeds [state your threshold, for example 5% or $25,000]. List the remaining lines in one sentence as within tolerance.

2. Cause, Not Description

  • For each material variance, state the cause in one sentence. “Revenue is $40,000 below budget” is a description, not a cause.
  • Separate timing differences from permanent differences, and volume effects from price or rate effects where the data allows.
  • Where the data does not show a cause, say so, and write the question the finance team must ask the budget owner.

3. Forward View

  • State which variances will reverse next month, which will continue, and the likely effect on the full-year outturn.
  • Flag any variance that suggests the budget assumption itself was wrong.

4. Executive Summary

  • Write a three-sentence summary a CEO can read in 20 seconds: the headline result, the biggest driver, and the one risk to watch.
  • Use numbers instead of adjectives. Do not write “significant”, “strong” or “challenging” without a figure next to it.

Deliver the commentary as a table with columns for Line, Actual, Budget, Variance, Cause and Outlook, followed by the executive summary and a list of open questions for budget owners. Do not invent figures. If a number is missing, mark it as missing.
summary: Explain monthly budget and prior-year variances with materiality thresholds, root causes, timing versus permanent effects, full-year outlook, and a CEO-ready summary.
title: Draft the variance commentary for your monthly management accounts
